---
title: "IR Schema"
---

The gridwell IR (Intermediate Representation) is a JSON document that fully describes a table's
structure, content, and styling.

## Design Principles

1. **Declarative** — describes *what* to render, not *how*
2. **Flat where possible** — uses indices/references, avoids deep nesting
3. **Typed values** — cells carry typed data alongside formatted text
4. **Styling by reference** — styles defined in a palette, referenced by ID
5. **Span-aware** — row/column spans are first-class with explicit placeholders
6. **Versioned** — `ir_version` allows future evolution

## Top-Level Structure

```json
{
  "ir_version": "1.0",
  "config": {...},
  "styles": {...},
  "header": {...},
  "column_spec": [...],
  "table": {...},
  "footer": {...},
  "extensions": {...}
}
```

<!-- ir-fields: Table -->

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `ir_version` | string | required | The IR version, `"1.0"` ([below](#versions)) |
| `config` | [Config](config.qmd) | required | Table-level configuration |
| `styles` | [StylePalette](styles.qmd#the-palette) | required | The style palette (`{}` for none) |
| `header` | [Header](header.qmd)? | `null` | Title, subtitle and extra header lines |
| `column_spec` | array of [ColumnSpec](columns.qmd) | required | One entry per column |
| `table` | [TableBlock](table-data.qmd) | required | The column labels and the body |
| `footer` | [Footer](footer.qmd)? | `null` | Footnotes and source notes |
| `extensions` | any? | `null` | Anything a producer wants to carry along. No writer reads it, and it round-trips unchanged; namespace its keys (`"example.com/producer"`) |

A field the IR doesn't have is ignored, so a table written for a newer minor version
still parses. Validation rejects a table whose values are wrong, not one with extra
fields.

## Versions

`ir_version` is `MAJOR.MINOR`: ASCII digits and a dot, nothing around them (`"01.00"`
reads as 1.0). A minor version only adds to the IR; a major version may change it.
This gridwell reads IR 1:

- **IR 1.0** is read as it is.
- **A newer minor version** (`"1.3"`) is read and rendered, with a
  [`NEWER_IR_VERSION` warning](validation.qmd#a-newer-minor-version): what that
  version added is left out. A field this gridwell doesn't know is ignored; a keyword
  value it doesn't know is an `UNKNOWN_VALUE` error, whose report notes the table's
  version.
- **Another major version** (`"2.0"`, `"0.9"`) is refused: an
  [`IR_VERSION`](validation.qmd#version) validation error, or, when the JSON doesn't
  parse as IR 1, a parse error saying the version is why.
- **Anything else** (`"1"`, `"1.0.0"`, `" 1.0"`) is an `IR_VERSION` error.

::: {.callout-note}
IR 1.0 is a **release candidate**. Until gridwell's first release, and the gt and
Great Tables emitters that write it, it may still change in a way that IR written
now doesn't survive. After that it is frozen: IR 1 only grows, by minor versions.
:::

## Content Nodes

Cell content is an array of content nodes, each an object whose `type` says which:

<!-- ir-content-nodes -->

| Type           | Fields              | Description                |
|----------------|---------------------|----------------------------|
| `text`         | `value`, `href`     | Plain text; `href` makes it a [link](../guide/output-formats.qmd#links) |
| `styled_text`  | `value`, `style_id`, `href` | Text with a style applied (`style_id` may be `null`) |
| `line_break`   | —                   | Line break within cell     |
| `footnote_mark`| `ref`, `mark_text`  | A footnote's mark: `ref` is the footnote's `id`, `mark_text` what is shown |
| `image`        | `src`, `alt`, `width`, `height` | Inline image ([below](#images)); `alt`, `width` and `height` may be `null` |
| `raw`          | `format`, `value`   | Markup for one format ([below](#raw-markup)) |

Every field is required except those that may be `null`, and `href`, which is
left out of a run that isn't a link. Only `http`, `https` and `mailto` URLs are
links ([`INVALID_HREF`](validation.qmd#structural-rules)), since a `javascript:` or
`file:` one could run code or open a local file when it is followed. A node of a `type` this
gridwell doesn't know parses, so a newer minor version can add node types: it is
drawn as nothing, and written back with all its fields when the IR is serialized
again.

## Raw markup

A `raw` node's `value` is markup in its `format` (`html`, `latex`, `typst`, `rtf`,
…), written as it is by that format's writer and dropped by the others. HTML is the
exception: every format draws it, by turning its inline markup (bold, italic,
colors, line breaks, images, …) into its own runs. The
[Output Formats](../guide/output-formats.qmd#raw-html) guide lists what is drawn.
Content may carry raw markup for several formats side by side (one version each);
then each writer takes only its own, HTML included.

Raw markup is a trust boundary. A writer copies it into its output unchecked, so
raw HTML can hold a script, and raw LaTeX, Typst or RTF can read files or run
commands when the output is compiled or opened. For IR you don't trust, render with
the [`raw` option](../guide/writer-options.qmd#options-of-every-format) off. Every
format takes it. Then every format draws raw HTML the way formats other than HTML
do, HTML included, and raw markup for other formats is dropped. An image's `src` is
another matter: HTML still writes it as it is (see [Images](#images)).

## Images

An `image` node's `src` is drawn only when it is a `data:` URI (base64 or
percent-encoded) holding a whole PNG, JPEG, GIF or SVG file. Writers never fetch a
URL or read a path named by `src`, as the IR may come from anywhere. HTML is the
exception: it writes `src` as given, and the browser loads it. An image a format
can't draw shows its `alt` text instead, and is [warned](validation.qmd#warnings) of.

`width` and `height` are CSS lengths, and an image is sized the way a browser sizes
an `<img>`. A side that is set is used. A side that isn't keeps the image's aspect
ratio, and with neither set the image keeps its own size (1px = 0.75pt). `em` is
relative to the text around the image.

| Format | Draws |
|--------|-------|
| HTML | any `src` |
| SVG, Typst | PNG, JPEG, GIF, SVG |
| DOCX | PNG, JPEG, GIF |
| RTF | PNG, JPEG |
| XLSX | PNG, JPEG, GIF, alone in its cell or line, but not in a footnote (it is drawn over the cell) |
| LaTeX, PPTX, ANSI | none (the alt text) |

Data that is whole but corrupt inside (a broken compressed stream, say) gets past
the check: depending on the format, the image may then show up blank, or the Typst
compiler may reject the document.
